arts.name: Shotokan Karate
arts.oneLiner: Funakoshi's linear power karate; the world's most widespread style.

arts.name: Goju-ryu Karate
arts.oneLiner: Miyagi's hard-soft Naha-te; close-range infighting with Sanchin breathing.

arts.name: Shito-ryu Karate
arts.oneLiner: Mabuni's fusion of Shuri speed and Naha power; biggest kata catalog.

arts.name: Wado-ryu Karate
arts.oneLiner: Otsuka's karate-plus-jujutsu; evasion and taisabaki over hard blocking.

arts.name: Kyokushin Karate
arts.oneLiner: Oyama's bare-knuckle knockdown karate; the original full-contact stand-up.

arts.name: Uechi-ryu Karate
arts.oneLiner: Most directly Chinese karate; crane-tiger circularity from Fujian Pangai-noon.

arts.name: Isshin-ryu Karate
arts.oneLiner: Shimabuku's vertical-fist synthesis; spread worldwide by US Marines.

arts.name: Taekwondo
arts.oneLiner: Korea's kick-dominant Olympic art; karate-rooted despite ancient-origin marketing (D).

arts.name: Tang Soo Do
arts.oneLiner: Hwang Kee's Shotokan-flavored Korean karate; popularized in US by Chuck Norris.

arts.name: Hapkido
arts.oneLiner: Korean aiki-jujutsu plus dynamic kicks; founder's Daito-ryu lineage disputed.

arts.name: American Kickboxing
arts.oneLiner: 1970s above-the-waist full-contact karate; boxing hands plus head/body kicks.

arts.name: Japanese Kickboxing / K-1
arts.oneLiner: Noguchi's karate-Muay Thai hybrid, reborn as Ishii's heavyweight K-1 in 1993.

arts.name: Sanda / Sanshou
arts.rootSource: Traditional kung fu + Shuai Jiao + boxing/judo
arts.oneLiner: China's full-contact sport: kickboxing plus catches, sweeps, and platform throws.

arts.name: Shuai Jiao
arts.rootSource: Jiao Li / Jiao Di military wrestling
arts.oneLiner: Ancient jacket wrestling; the genuinely pressure-tested root of CMA clinch.

arts.name: Shaolin Kung Fu
arts.oneLiner: Umbrella temple brand; Bodhidharma origin is debunked myth, athletics are real.

arts.name: Wing Chun
arts.oneLiner: Centerline close-range trapping; Ip Man and Bruce Lee made it famous.

arts.name: Hung Gar
arts.oneLiner: Tiger-crane southern power; Wong Fei-hung's rooted iron-body kung fu.

arts.name: Choy Li Fut
arts.rootSource: Choy Gar + Li Gar + Fut Gar synthesis
arts.oneLiner: Precisely dated 1836 synthesis; windmill strikes keeping long-range mobility.

arts.name: Praying Mantis (Tanglangquan)
arts.oneLiner: Hook-hand trapping chains; Wang Lang origin and dating are contested.

arts.name: Bak Mei
arts.oneLiner: Hakka six-power explosive short-range; named for myth-traitor white-browed monk.

arts.name: Drunken Boxing (Zui Quan)
arts.rootSource: Shaolin ditangquan & Daoist Eight Immortals lore
arts.oneLiner: Method not school; staggering deception demanding exceptional sobriety and balance.

arts.name: Modern Competitive Wushu
arts.oneLiner: 20th-c. state sport: Taolu is performance, Sanda is real combat.

arts.name: Tai Chi Chuan
arts.oneLiner: Internal flagship; Chen-rooted, mostly health practice, humbled by Xu Xiaodong.

arts.name: Baguazhang
arts.oneLiner: Circle-walking palm art; mobility and angles over linear force.

arts.name: Xingyiquan
arts.rootSource: Ming spear method distilled to empty hand
arts.oneLiner: Linear five-element fists; spear logic empty-handed, Yue Fei credit is myth.

arts.name: Qigong
arts.era: Daoyin Tu c.168 BCE; term 20th c.
arts.oneLiner: Breath-energy substrate beneath internal CMA; real benefits, fraudulent qi claims.

arts.name: Jeet Kune Do
arts.oneLiner: Bruce Lee's 1967 style-of-no-style; conceptual ancestor of modern MMA.

arts.name: Muay Thai
arts.oneLiner: Brutally effective eight-limb striking; battlefield art turned global ring sport.

arts.name: Lethwei
arts.oneLiner: Bare-knuckle nine-limb striking with headbutts; KO-or-draw brutality.

arts.name: Pradal Serey
arts.era: roots claimed 1st c. CE; early 20th c.
arts.oneLiner: Cambodia's elbow-forward kickboxing cousin of Muay Thai.

arts.name: Bokator
arts.oneLiner: Cambodia's full battlefield system of animal styles, weapons, and ground.

arts.name: Vovinam
arts.oneLiner: Vietnam's nationalist all-rounder famed for flying-scissor leg takedowns.

arts.name: Pencak Silat
arts.oneLiner: Sprawling Malay blade-and-footwork family; keris, kerambit, tiger-low Harimau.

arts.name: Filipino Eskrima / Arnis / Kali
arts.rootSource: indigenous blade arts + Spanish espada y daga
arts.oneLiner: Weapon-first stick-and-blade art; world's premier practical armed self-defense.

arts.name: Kalaripayattu
arts.era: system c.11th-12th c. CE; 'oldest' claim is myth (D)
arts.oneLiner: Kerala's flexible-blade and vital-point art; 'oldest martial art' claim is myth.

arts.name: Silambam
arts.oneLiner: Ancient Tamil bamboo-staff art with Sangam-literature provenance.

arts.name: Gatka
arts.oneLiner: Sikh rhythmic sword-and-shield art; sporting face of battlefield Shastar Vidya.

arts.name: Thang-Ta
arts.oneLiner: Manipur's Meitei sword-and-spear art, dance-adjacent and colonial-suppressed.

arts.name: Angampora
arts.oneLiner: Sri Lanka's near-lost coiled-blade and vital-point art, colonial-suppressed and revived.

arts.name: Classical Jujutsu (Koryu)
arts.oneLiner: Battlefield jujutsu koryu; the genetic root of judo and aikido.

arts.name: Judo
arts.oneLiner: Kano's 1882 rationalized jujutsu; randori-driven throwing art and Olympic sport.

arts.name: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu
arts.oneLiner: Ground-dominant judo offshoot; inverted Kano's throw focus toward guard and submissions.

arts.name: Aikido
arts.oneLiner: Ueshiba's harmony-focused aiki art derived from Daito-ryu aiki-jujutsu.

arts.name: Daito-ryu Aiki-jujutsu
arts.oneLiner: Takeda's dense aiki branch of jujutsu; parent of aikido and hapkido.

arts.name: Sumo
arts.oneLiner: Japan's ritual ring-wrestling; explosive clinch and off-balance, no ground.

arts.name: Kenjutsu & Kendo
arts.oneLiner: Samurai swordsmanship and its armored sparring sport descendant.

arts.name: Iaido
arts.oneLiner: Solo art of drawing and cutting in one decisive motion.

arts.name: Naginata-do
arts.oneLiner: Glaive art of reach and leverage; classical and armored-sport forms.

arts.name: Bojutsu
arts.oneLiner: Staff and stick arts emphasizing range, leverage, and improvised-weapon skill.

arts.name: Kyudo
arts.oneLiner: Meditative samurai longbow art; standing-Zen form with no combat use today.

arts.name: Olympic Freestyle Wrestling
arts.oneLiner: Olympic codification of catch wrestling; legal-leg takedowns and pinning.

arts.name: Greco-Roman Wrestling
arts.oneLiner: French upper-body-only code; high-amplitude suplexes, no leg attacks.

arts.name: American Folkstyle Wrestling
arts.oneLiner: US school code rewarding riding time, control, and accumulated near-falls.

arts.name: Catch Wrestling
arts.oneLiner: Aggressive English pin-or-submit wrestling; ancestral root of MMA hooking.

arts.name: Sambo & Combat Sambo
arts.oneLiner: Soviet judo-plus-folk synthesis; leglock-heavy sport, MMA-like Combat variant.

arts.name: Mongolian Bokh
arts.oneLiner: Steppe standing wrestling; no weight class, touch-ground loses.

arts.name: Turkish Yagli Gures
arts.oneLiner: Olive-oiled Turkish wrestling; world's oldest continuous sporting festival.

arts.name: Kushti / Pehlwani
arts.oneLiner: Mughal clay-pit wrestling; total-lifestyle akhara conditioning under a guru.

arts.name: Iranian Pahlavani / Koshti
arts.oneLiner: Persian heroic wrestling tied to the spiritual Zurkhaneh House of Strength.

arts.name: Icelandic Glima
arts.oneLiner: Nordic belt-grip wrestling; upright constant motion, technique over strength.

arts.name: Swiss Schwingen
arts.oneLiner: Swiss Alpine jute-trouser wrestling; throw onto back in sawdust ring.

arts.name: Senegalese Laamb
arts.oneLiner: Senegalese sand wrestling; the laamb variant uniquely permits bare-fist strikes.

arts.name: Nuba Wrestling
arts.oneLiner: Ash-coated Sudanese festival wrestling; throw and pin opponent on his back.

arts.name: Cornish / Lancashire / Collar-and-Elbow
arts.oneLiner: British-Isles folk wrestling family; ancestral pool of freestyle, folkstyle and catch.

arts.name: Boxing
arts.oneLiner: Among the most battle-tested striking arts on Earth; hands only, drilled deep.

arts.name: Bare-Knuckle Boxing
arts.oneLiner: Boxing's bare-fisted ancestor, revived state-sanctioned by BKFC in 2018.

arts.name: Savate
arts.oneLiner: French foot-fighting that kicks with the shoe; carries cane and staff siblings.

arts.name: HEMA Longsword (Liechtenauer)
arts.oneLiner: Reconstructed German longsword from Liechtenauer's cryptic verse and its glosses.

arts.name: HEMA Armizare (Fiore dei Liberi)
arts.oneLiner: Reconstructed Italian art of arms spanning wrestling, dagger, sword, poleaxe, horse.

arts.name: HEMA Sword & Buckler (MS I.33)
arts.rootSource: Royal Armouries MS I.33, oldest European fightbook
arts.oneLiner: World's oldest surviving European combat manual; priest, scholar, and Walpurgis.

arts.name: HEMA Ringen
arts.rootSource: Ott Jud, Talhoffer, Auerswald wrestling treatises
arts.oneLiner: Reconstructed medieval German wrestling — sportive throws and combat joint-breaks.

arts.name: Olympic Fencing
arts.rootSource: Renaissance Italian rapier, refined by French school
arts.oneLiner: Sportified blade-play with elite timing; safest art here to spar hard.

arts.name: Bartitsu
arts.rootSource: jujitsu + boxing + savate + Vigny la canne
arts.oneLiner: Victorian eclectic self-defense; the 'Sherlock Holmes' art and proto-MMA.

arts.name: Jogo do Pau
arts.rootSource: rural staff use; Lisbon urban school
arts.oneLiner: Portuguese staff art with intact lineage, built to fight multiple opponents.

arts.name: Defendu
arts.oneLiner: Shanghai-forged combatives that became WWII Commando and OSS hand-to-hand.

arts.name: Mixed Martial Arts
arts.rootSource: Synthesis of BJJ, wrestling, Muay Thai, boxing
arts.oneLiner: The empirical proving ground; styles collide until the optimum emerges.

arts.name: Vale Tudo
arts.rootSource: Circus challenge matches; Maeda's judo via Gracies
arts.oneLiner: MMA's brutal Brazilian ancestor; the original style-versus-style crucible.

arts.name: Capoeira
arts.oneLiner: Afro-Brazilian combat-dance of deception, spinning kicks, and the berimbau roda.

arts.name: Engolo
arts.oneLiner: Angolan inverted-kicking circle game; capoeira's contested African ancestor.

arts.name: Dambe
arts.oneLiner: Hausa one-fisted boxing with the corded 'spear' hand from harvest festivals.

arts.name: Kapu Kuialua (Lua)
arts.oneLiner: Hawaiian bone-breaking warrior art, suppressed then revived in the 1970s.

arts.name: Okichitaw
arts.oneLiner: Modern reconstruction of Plains Cree warfare on a judo-hapkido frame.

arts.name: Xilam
arts.oneLiner: Modern Mexican striking art on Mesoamerican symbolism and a Kempo base.

arts.name: Pankration
arts.oneLiner: Greece's no-rules strike-and-grapple sport, ancient MMA prototype.

arts.name: Greek Pygmachia & Pale
arts.oneLiner: Olympic boxing and wrestling, evidenced from Minoan frescoes onward.

arts.name: Roman Military & Gladiatorial Combat
arts.oneLiner: Disciplined gladius drill and arena spectacle, well-excavated.

arts.name: Egyptian Wrestling (Beni Hasan)
arts.oneLiner: World's oldest illustrated grappling system, painted at Beni Hasan.

arts.name: Egyptian Tahtib
arts.oneLiner: Ancient Egyptian staff-fighting surviving as living Nile folk art.

arts.name: Mesopotamian/Sumerian Grappling
arts.rootSource: Sumerian belt wrestling; Epic of Gilgamesh
arts.oneLiner: Belt-grip wrestling fixed by a 2600 BC bronze and Gilgamesh.

arts.name: Indian Malla-yuddha & Vajra-Mushti
arts.era: Malla Purana c.13th c.; Agni Purana 8th-11th c.
arts.oneLiner: India's combat-wrestling and thunderbolt-fist, documented in medieval manuals.

arts.name: Chinese Jiao Li / Jiao Di
arts.era: Classic of Rites c.3rd-1st c. BC
arts.oneLiner: China's military throwing art, from horn-butting to Shuai Jiao.

arts.name: Japanese Ancient Sumo (Sumai)
arts.oneLiner: Japan's ritual grappling, legendary at 23 BC, attested by 642 AD.

arts.name: Norse Glima & Holmgang
arts.oneLiner: Norse jacket-wrestling and the ox-hide judicial duel, holmgang.

arts.name: Mesoamerican Ritual Combat
arts.oneLiner: Aztec tethered-captive sacrifice combat, a spectacle of asymmetric death.

arts.name: Persian/Parthian Pahlavani
arts.oneLiner: Persia's house-of-strength wrestling, tracing heroes to the Parthians.

arts.name: Korean Subak / Taekkyeon
arts.oneLiner: Korea's fluid kicking-tripping folk art, anchored in Goguryeo murals.

arts.name: Kill or Get Killed (Applegate/OSS)
arts.oneLiner: Applegate's 1943 OSS manual Americanizing Fairbairn's killing methods and point shooting.

arts.name: LINE
arts.oneLiner: USMC lethal-default linear system; its no-continuum flaw birthed MCMAP.

arts.name: MCMAP
arts.rootSource: karate, judo, taekwondo, boxing, jujutsu, LINE
arts.oneLiner: Belt-based USMC program adding a force continuum LINE lacked.

arts.name: MACP (Modern Army Combatives)
arts.rootSource: Gracie/BJJ, wrestling, judo, boxing, Muay Thai
arts.oneLiner: BJJ-anchored Army MMA synthesis built on positional dominance and live training.

arts.name: SOCP (Special Operations Combatives)
arts.rootSource: BJJ, wrestling, Sayoc Kali, weapon retention
arts.oneLiner: SOF system for fighting in armor while retaining and accessing the weapon.

arts.name: Krav Maga
arts.oneLiner: Documented IDF self-defense system; quality varies wildly by school.

arts.name: KAPAP
arts.oneLiner: Genuine pre-1948 program; modern version is a rebrand/reconstruction.

arts.name: Hisardut
arts.oneLiner: Karate-judo-jujutsu fusion by Dennis Hanover; deeper but less widespread.

arts.name: Systema
arts.oneLiner: Cossack and Spetsnaz claims are marketing-myth; no competition record.

arts.name: British Commando Close-Combat
arts.oneLiner: Fairbairn-Sykes WWII combatives; documented, simple, lethal.

arts.name: Defendo
arts.oneLiner: Underwood's Canadian WWII combatives; practical, control-oriented, well-documented.

arts.name: Modern PMC / Close-Protection
arts.oneLiner: Professional protection curriculum; serious end pressure-tested, thin hand-to-hand.

arts.name: Reality-Based Self-Defense (RBSD)
arts.oneLiner: Category prioritizing real assaults; best layered on a resisted base.

arts.name: MGS CQC (Close Quarters Combat)
arts.rootSource: WWII Fairbairn/Applegate combatives + judo/aikido/jiu-jitsu + weapon retention
arts.oneLiner: Real WWII combatives and judo, scaffolded by a SWAT consultant for spectacle.

arts.name: Sifu (Pak Mei)
arts.rootSource: Pak Mei (Bak Mei) southern kung fu
arts.oneLiner: Pak Mei master Benjamin Colussi choreographed unusually authentic short-power kung fu.

arts.name: Sleeping Dogs Brawling
arts.oneLiner: Wing Chun and JKD vocabulary packaged as flowy Hong Kong combat cinema.

arts.name: Tekken Styles
arts.rootSource: Per-character real arts: Shotokan, lucha, TKD, vale tudo, judo
arts.oneLiner: Real style identities like lucha and TKD over fantasy juggle physics.

arts.name: Virtua Fighter Styles
arts.rootSource: Per-character real arts: Bajiquan, Mizongquan, Muay Thai, aiki-jujutsu
arts.oneLiner: Obscure-but-real styles and honest physics make it the genre's most accurate.

arts.name: Dead or Alive Styles
arts.rootSource: Named real arts loosely held: JKD, Piguaquan, Taiji, pro wrestling
arts.oneLiner: Real style names, but Itagaki openly chose fun over authenticity.

arts.name: Absolver Combat
arts.rootSource: Composite kung fu/striking fusion, drunken boxing
arts.oneLiner: Grounded combat principles wrapped in invented composite stances and decks.

arts.name: The Last of Us (Survival Violence)
arts.oneLiner: Improvised, brutal, fast survival violence truer in spirit than most arts games.

arts.name: Splinter Cell (Krav Maga)
arts.rootSource: Krav Maga (+ Systema, Kali, jiu-jitsu in lore)
arts.oneLiner: Krav Maga chosen for quick, brutal, ruleless efficiency a real operative would use.

arts.name: Yakuza (Dragon of Dojima)
arts.rootSource: Kyokushin karate + boxing + judo + pro wrestling
arts.oneLiner: Believable Kyokushin brawler-with-throws under absurd cinematic heat finishers.

arts.name: For Honor (Weapon Styles)
arts.rootSource: HEMA longsword + kenjutsu + Viking weapon combat
arts.oneLiner: Directional guards abstract a real HEMA truth atop fantasy durability.

arts.name: John Wick Gun-Fu
arts.rootSource: Judo + Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu + 3-Gun/combat shooting (CAR attribution disputed)
arts.oneLiner: Judo/BJJ + 3-Gun shooting; the 'Center Axis Relock' label is popular but disputed.

arts.name: Jason Bourne Style
arts.oneLiner: Jeff Imada's Kali + JKD; improvised-weapon realism over stylized spectacle.

arts.name: Bruce Lee / JKD Films
arts.rootSource: Jeet Kune Do (Wing Chun + boxing + fencing)
arts.oneLiner: Bruce Lee's own art on screen; fast, economical, philosophically real.

arts.name: Ip Man / Wing Chun Films
arts.rootSource: Wing Chun (choreographer Sammo Hung; consultant Ip Chun)
arts.oneLiner: Real Wing Chun trapping, cinematically accelerated into chain-punch spectacle.

arts.name: Ong-Bak / Tony Jaa (Muay Boran)
arts.oneLiner: Authentic Muay Boran: 'no wires, no CGI, no stunt doubles.'

arts.name: The Raid (Pencak Silat)
arts.rootSource: Pencak Silat (Iko Uwais & Yayan Ruhian, real practitioners)
arts.oneLiner: Real Silat masters choreograph brutal close-quarters blade-and-empty-hand combat.

arts.name: Jackie Chan (Acrobatic HK / Drunken)
arts.rootSource: Peking opera + Zui Quan (drunken boxing) + acrobatics
arts.oneLiner: Real opera-trained acrobatics and props; choreography exaggerated for comedy.

arts.name: Avatar: The Last Airbender (Bending)
arts.rootSource: CMA-mapped: Tai Chi, Hung Gar, Northern Shaolin, Baguazhang, Chu Gar (consultant Sifu Kisu)
arts.oneLiner: Each element is a real CMA style faithfully mocapped; only the powers are fantasy.

arts.name: Baki the Grappler
arts.rootSource: Karate, judo, BJJ, boxing, Muay Thai, vale tudo, pro wrestling
arts.oneLiner: Real arts and real-fighter homages with deliberately superhuman execution.

arts.name: Kenichi: The Mightiest Disciple
arts.rootSource: Each master a real style: Muay Thai, karate, jujutsu, Chinese kenpo, weapons
arts.oneLiner: Educational survey of real styles, each master a distinct discipline.

arts.name: Hajime no Ippo
arts.rootSource: Western boxing (author Morikawa was a cornerman/journalist)
arts.oneLiner: The most technically realistic fight series: real boxing science, real punches.

arts.name: Megalo Box
arts.rootSource: Boxing + sci-fi powered 'Gear' exoskeletons (Ashita no Joe homage)
arts.oneLiner: Exoskeleton boxing; faithful as homage to Ashita no Joe, not as boxing realism.

arts.name: Kengan Ashura
arts.rootSource: Named real arts (Aikido, Taiho-jutsu, Goju-ryu, judo, boxing, sumo); author is a martial artist
arts.oneLiner: Well-researched named real styles, openly stylized to superhuman 'Removal' feats.

arts.name: Naruto Gentle Fist (Juken)
arts.rootSource: Resembles Baguazhang (Eight Trigrams); Tier C for authorial intent
arts.oneLiner: Hyuga palm-strikes echo Baguazhang's Eight Trigrams, atop a fantasy chakra system.
